overall_summary: Geopolitical escalations from US-Iran strikes and wider Middle East conflicts are driving clear risk-off pressure, with Bitcoin testing support near 63k amid liquidations. ETF inflows and fading panic sales provide some offset, but Strategy's buy pause, elevated yields, and a firm dollar keep the tone heavy. Today's CPI release remains the key near-term catalyst.
key_points: US-Iran and ME conflicts fuel risk-off
Bitcoin tests 63k support with heavy liquidations
ETFs post first inflows after eight-week streak
Strategy pauses BTC buys for cash cushion
CPI data and Fed testimony due today

items.title: US Gov Moves $288M Seized BTC and ETH to Coinbase Prime
items.summary: US government wallets transferred roughly 3,800 bitcoin and 30,000 ether worth about 288 million dollars to Coinbase Prime from older seizure cases including BTC-e and others. Bitcoin went through intermediate wallets while ether moved directly. This comes despite a Trump-era executive order creating a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve that directs seized bitcoin not to be sold. Traders should care because exchange deposits often precede sales and this could add unexpected supply even if it is only a small fraction of total government holdings.
items.impact: Risk of liquidation adding sell pressure

items.title: US-Iran Airstrikes Drive Risk-Off as Bitcoin Slides Near 63k
items.summary: Bitcoin dropped more than one percent to hover near 63,000 dollars amid renewed mutual airstrikes between the US and Iran that raised fears over Strait of Hormuz shipping. Brent crude jumped over three percent adding inflation concerns just ahead of CPI data. This revived risk-off selling that has hit crypto in prior oil shocks. Traders need to watch because geopolitics can overwhelm technicals and ETF flows in the short term while lifting Fed rate-hike bets.
items.impact: Macro downside pressure and higher volatility

items.title: Strategy Pauses Bitcoin Buys and Builds 3 Billion Cash Cushion
items.summary: Michael Saylor's Strategy has bought no bitcoin since June 22 and earlier sold 3,588 BTC for about 216 million dollars. It raised roughly 467 million via stock sales last week lifting its USD reserve to 3 billion dollars which covers over 20 months of preferred dividends and debt interest. Holdings sit unchanged at 843,775 BTC. This matters because Strategy has been one of the largest and steadiest corporate buyers so the pause removes a key demand source during a weak market.

items.title: Bitcoin ETFs Break Eight-Week Outflow Streak with Weekly Inflows
items.summary: Spot bitcoin ETFs posted about 197 million dollars in net inflows last week ending an eight-week streak of outflows that drained billions. Ether funds also flipped positive. Monday July 13 itself saw roughly 425 million in outflows led by major funds. The weekly turnaround signals some institutional demand returning even as price remains under pressure. Traders should track whether this becomes a sustained trend that can absorb selling and support a base near current levels.
items.impact: Positive demand catalyst if inflows continue

items.title: Bitcoin Panic Selling May Be Ending as Net Sales Collapse
items.summary: On-chain data shows spot net selling slowed from nearly 2,000 BTC per day in June to just 53 BTC a day so far in July. Bitcoin held near 62,000 dollars through weekend US-Iran escalations and oil spikes where earlier similar events caused sharp drops. Combined with the ETF inflow reversal this points to weak-hand exhaustion. Traders care because seller fatigue often precedes bottoms especially if spot demand reappears ahead of CPI and other macro data.
items.impact: Reduced sell-side pressure supporting a potential floor

items.title: Hundreds of Millions Liquidated as Bitcoin Tests Support
items.summary: Crypto liquidations totaled around 250 to 300 million dollars in the past 24 hours with the majority long positions as bitcoin slipped below 63,000. Thousands of traders were wiped out amid the risk-off move. This leverage flush often cleans the market of overextended positions. Traders should note that while painful short-term it can reduce forced selling and set up cleaner moves once macro or geopolitical noise settles.
items.impact: Leverage reset that may stabilize price after washout

items.title: US June CPI Data Due Today at 8:30 AM ET
items.summary: The Bureau of Labor Statistics releases the Consumer Price Index for June today. Consensus looks for a cool-down to 3.8 percent year-over-year from 4.2 percent previously, with core expected near 2.8 percent. Traders should care because this is the key inflation print that will drive Treasury yields, Fed rate-hike odds, the dollar, and risk assets including Bitcoin in the hours and days ahead. A hotter number would reinforce higher-for-longer rates while a cooler one could ease pressure.
items.impact: High volatility and potential directional move in yields, DXY, and crypto depending on the print

items.title: NFIB Small Business Optimism Jumps to 97.4 in June
items.summary: The NFIB Small Business Optimism Index rose 2.1 points to 97.4 in June, beating the 95.8 consensus and approaching its long-term average. Expectations for better business conditions and sales drove the gain, though inflation remains the top problem for owners and price hikes are still elevated. Crypto traders should watch this because stronger small-business confidence supports the soft-landing narrative and risk appetite, even as sticky inflation keeps Fed caution alive.
items.impact: Supportive for equities and risk assets if it signals resilient economy without overheating

items.title: 10-Year Treasury Yield Holds Near 4.63% Multi-Week Highs
items.summary: The US 10-year yield is trading around 4.62 to 4.63 percent, near two-month highs, as Middle East tensions push oil higher and lift inflation and rate-hike concerns. Markets now price about a 51 percent chance of a Fed hike in September. Higher yields raise the cost of capital and typically pressure Bitcoin and growth assets, so this remains a key headwind until the CPI or Fed comments change the narrative.
items.impact: Pressure on risk assets and crypto via tighter financial conditions

items.title: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh Testifies Before Congress Today
items.summary: New Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh delivers testimony on the semi-annual monetary policy report to the House Financial Services Committee starting around 10 AM ET. Markets will parse every word for clues on the inflation outlook, rate path, and response to oil-driven price pressures. Any hawkish tilt could reinforce yield gains and dollar strength, while dovish notes might give risk assets breathing room.
items.impact: Potential catalyst for yields, DXY, and crypto depending on tone

items.title: US June Budget Deficit Hits $120 Billion on Tariff Refunds
items.summary: The Treasury reported a $120 billion federal budget deficit for June, narrower than the prior month's $293 billion but a sharp swing from last June's surplus, driven by nearly $50 billion in tariff refunds after legal rulings. Cumulative deficits remain large. Fiscal news like this can influence long-term yields and dollar sentiment if markets worry about debt sustainability, which matters for crypto as a potential alternative asset.
items.impact: Mild fiscal concern that could support higher term premium in yields

items.title: US Dollar Index Holds Near 101 Amid Geopolitical Jitters
items.summary: The DXY is trading around 101, supported by Middle East tensions, higher oil prices, and rising Treasury yields that boost rate differentials. A firm dollar typically acts as a headwind for Bitcoin and commodities. Traders should monitor whether the greenback extends gains post-CPI or fades if inflation cools, as DXY strength often correlates with risk-off moves in crypto.
items.impact: Headwind for Bitcoin and other risk assets via stronger USD

items.title: US-Iran Strikes Escalate Over Strait of Hormuz Control
items.summary: The United States and Iran have exchanged multiple nights of strikes, with US forces hitting Iranian military targets and Iran's Revolutionary Guard hitting US bases in Bahrain, Kuwait, Jordan and elsewhere. Trump has reinstated a blockade on Iranian shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, claimed US guardianship of the waterway, and floated a 20 percent toll on vessels. This chokepoint handles about a fifth of global oil trade, so any prolonged disruption drives energy prices higher and fuels risk-off sentiment across markets including crypto.
items.impact: Oil price spikes, inflation fears, and broad risk-asset selloffs

items.title: Russia Extends Diesel Export Ban Amid Refinery Attacks
items.summary: Russia has banned diesel and related fuel exports through the end of July after Ukrainian drone strikes hammered its refineries, creating domestic shortages and long gas lines. The move has already tightened global diesel supplies and pushed prices higher, layering onto Hormuz tensions. Crypto traders should watch because higher industrial fuel costs feed into inflation and can pressure risk assets while boosting energy-related volatility.
items.impact: Global fuel supply crunch and higher energy inflation

items.title: Ukraine Hits Over 100 Russian Shadow Fleet Tankers
items.summary: Ukrainian drones have struck dozens more vessels in Russia's shadow fleet used to evade oil sanctions, bringing the total to over 100 ships hit in about eight days, mainly in the Sea of Azov. This compounds Russia's fuel crisis and further disrupts sanctioned oil flows. The continued degradation of Russian energy export capacity adds to global supply risks and keeps geopolitical premium in oil prices elevated.
items.impact: Further pressure on Russian oil logistics and energy prices

items.title: Senator Lindsey Graham Dies; Sister Named to Seat
items.summary: Republican Senator Lindsey Graham of South Carolina has died at 71 after a brief illness, shortly after visiting Ukraine. The governor has appointed his sister Darline Graham Nordone to fill the seat until a special election. While mostly a domestic political story, Graham was a strong voice for military aid and hawkish foreign policy, so the succession could subtly shift Senate dynamics on Ukraine and Middle East issues.
items.impact: Limited near-term market move; potential foreign-policy nuance

items.title: Israeli Settlers Detain US Congressman in West Bank
items.summary: Armed Israeli settlers detained Democratic Congressman Ro Khanna and his delegation for about 90 minutes while visiting a destroyed Palestinian village, and separately attacked journalists. The incidents highlight rising settler violence in the occupied West Bank amid broader regional tensions. Traders should note any further escalation could draw US political pressure and add another layer of Middle East instability on top of the Iran conflict.
items.impact: Heightened regional tension risk but secondary to Hormuz

items.title: Houthis Strike Saudi Airport as Regional Fires Spread
items.summary: Yemen's Houthis launched missiles and drones at Saudi Arabia's Abha airport in a sharp escalation. This comes as the wider Middle East conflict involving Iran and the US intensifies. Additional proxy attacks raise the chance of broader Gulf involvement, which could further threaten energy infrastructure and shipping lanes beyond Hormuz itself.
items.impact: Expanded regional risk premium on oil and risk assets
